segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Honest. I think she'll like that better than a promise.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Every Warden song I know ends at a door like this. None of them say what's behind it. That ought to worry me more.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Lovely. I'll put that in the chorus.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Somebody woke them before we got here. And somebody is still here.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Ah. Well. They know we're here, then.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Nothing has touched these. No fire at all. Do you know how rare that is in this Vale?

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Every hearth. Every forge. Every ember-lamp in every window, for three hundred years.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: That's why the songs are all that's left. Nobody ever needed a fire to remember a tune.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Your archivist begged for records the fire never touched. Well, here they are. He won't thank you for them.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: You knew. You chose. Ysolde told you the price to your face, which makes her the most honest thing in this whole Vale.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Somebody's. Somebody who was never asked either. It turns out we've all been paying with other people's memories.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: No. They lit the lamps and warmed their hands, and nobody ever told them there was a bill.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Marrowby. Celandine Marrowby. She's older than anyone in Emberwick, and remembers less than any of them.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: A hundred years of ember-lamps in every hall she owns. She's burned that night away. She doesn't know what she did.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Then you've a choice to make. Truth is heavy. Gold's heavier, if you're the one carrying it.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Mother Aubrine will need you to say that gently. And then she'll need you to say it again.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: The gods might well agree. The Wardens don't seem to have asked them.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: You and Corvin found it twice and lost it twice. This time it's on a page no fire has ever touched.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Then hold on to it. You may be the only one of us who'll notice when something goes missing.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: I'm going to write a song about this. Nobody is going to want to hear it.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: They don't remember their own names, but they remember the tune. Songs don't burn. I did tell you.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: There you are. Twenty years I've followed you across this Vale, and you've never once let me catch up.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: My teacher's teacher kept a Warden songbook from before the Fall. Beside the Song of the Seven, someone drew a face in the margin. That face.
